title: How Blest, Amid All Blessing
description: How Blest, Amid All Blessing in Tonic Solfa to GREENLAND, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Greenleaf Adams wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 784 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to GREENLAND; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: How blest, a-mid all bless-ing This chang-ing world be-stows, That soul in truth pos-sess-ing Pi-ty for o-thers' woes; Rea-dy to move and light-en The load a-fflic-tion bears Want's face with joy to bright-en, In deed, as with its prayers.

lines: Want's face with joy to brighten,
In deed, as with its prayers.
Thus Christ, the Friend and Servant
And those who in his spirit
Would seek to live and move,
God of all times and stations!

licence: Public domain: John Greenleaf Adams died in 1887.
credits: Words by John Greenleaf Adams (1810–1887), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to GREENLAND by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
